research.summary: Unverified (I could not open any JTA or news page because this session's network allowlist blocks those hosts, so I saw them only as search-engine extracts): the JTA Skyway carries no passengers today. JTA suspended all Skyway passenger service indefinitely as part of its FY2027 budget cuts. The pause was planned for the Nov. 2, 2026 service changes, with the last scheduled run on Friday evening, Oct. 30, but staffing problems ended service early on the morning of Friday, Oct. 30, 2026; no part of the line runs and no reopening date has been announced. All eight stations are closed, including the LaVilla platform at the JRTC (found fenced off), and the JRTC has no other rail service (Amtrak still uses its Clifford Lane station); the NAVI autonomous vans on the Bay Street Innovation Corridor run at street level, not on the Skyway guideway.

research.open_questions:
1) Verification gap: none of the JTA or news pages could be opened. Every real-world status claim above rests on search-engine extracts (opened=false), and those quotes may differ slightly from the live pages. Before these decisions are applied, jtafla.com (service alerts, the Skyway page, the budget press release) should be opened. To do that, jtafla.com, www.actionnewsjax.com, jaxtoday.org and www.news4jax.com would have to be allowed in the session's network settings. I changed no settings. The only page I opened was live OSM data from the Overpass API.
2) Dates agree once read closely. The press release and news describe the pause as starting 'Nov. 2'. JTA's own statement says operations were 'scheduled to pause Friday evening' (Oct. 30) as part of the Nov. 2 changes, and that staffing problems ended service on Friday morning, Oct. 30. JTA's site banner says service 'concluded early today, October 30'. A search extract of Wikipedia's Skyway infobox also gives the closure date as Oct. 30, 2026. No source suggests that any segment still runs, and I found no bus bridge set up for this shutdown.
3) What happens to the guideway: JTA calls this a pause while the system's future is decided. A Jacksonville Today extract says JTA's CEO told the FTA in February 2026 that talks on the Skyway's remaining useful life had begun. The 2026 study (PD&E) alternatives include rehabilitation, new automated people-mover trains, a trail with autonomous vehicles at street level, and demolition; News4JAX put the costs at $151.95M to $565.44M. JTA postponed the second round of public meetings in May 2026. No decision on a replacement was found.
4) NAVI (U2C phase 1, the Bay Street Innovation Corridor) context: its vans run at street level on Bay Street, from Pearl Street to EverBank Stadium, with 12 stops, weekdays 7am to 7pm. They never used the Skyway guideway; the phase 2 plan to convert the guideway with ramps was only studied. Sources disagree on when NAVI ends: Jan. 1, 2027 (Action News Jax, News4JAX), 'beginning Dec.' (Jacksonville Today, Sept. 17), or Dec. 31, 2026 (a Wikipedia extract). One report says the autonomous software licence is expiring, so the vans would revert to manual driving. Search summaries conflict on whether NAVI has a stop at the JRTC, so that is unconfirmed.
5) Other rail at the JRTC: none. Amtrak still serves Jacksonville from Clifford Lane. Moving it to LaVilla is one of eight JAX FAST master-planning projects, with no design or timeline yet (source date not seen).
6) OSM: changeset 191257956 at 2026-10-30T22:31:45Z added disused:railway=station to the seven station nodes, which still also carry railway=station. The JRTC node 8427291139 (last edited 2022-01-21) and its stop_area relation 12322087 were not touched. The JRTC's LaVilla stop positions 8427291021 and 8427291022 and the Skyway track ways are tagged disused, as are the Northbank route relations (disused=yes). So the JRTC node's missing disused tag looks like an editing omission, not evidence of service.

research.summary: UNVERIFIED: no page could be opened in this session, so every source below is a search-engine excerpt (opened=false). The excerpts say the APT has carried no passengers since 29 August 2020, when its owner-operator, the Dallas County Utility and Reclamation District (DCURD), suspended all passenger service because of COVID-19; the district's website reads 'THE APT SYSTEM IS CLOSED INDEFINITELY', and no source reports a reopening up to November 2026. research.summary: Metro Rail is carrying passengers. Since 1 November 2026 NFTA has run it on one track in two zones (Humboldt-Hospital to Allen/Medical Campus underground, Church to Canalside above ground), with a train about every 20 minutes and trains ending at Canalside because DL&W station is temporarily closed until about mid- to late November 2026. The other 13 stations are served, several from one platform only, including Seneca and Canalside (the former Erie Canal Harbor, which reopened under the new name on 2 July 2024); DL&W first opened to passengers on 8 December 2025. research.reason:
UNCERTAIN: I could neither verify nor refute this conclusion, because I could not open any source.

(1) Blocked sites. WebFetch to www.jtafla.com, www.actionnewsjax.com and www.news4jax.com failed with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND, meaning those hosts are outside this session's allowed network domains. These were network blocks, not bot checks or captchas. The tool said that when several hosts fail this way I should stop trying more sites and not re-fetch the failed ones until they are allowed. So I did not try jaxtoday.org, www.yahoo.com, jtafla.com or maps.mail.ru.

(2) No independent search. Every WebSearch call returned "web search budget is used up". That limit is 200 calls per turn, shared by all agents in the workflow. So I found no operator alerts, board or council minutes, or local news of my own, and no newer or contrary evidence.

(3) The conclusion itself is unverified at its foundation. Every JTA and news item it cites is opened=false, seen only as a search-engine extract. The only items marked opened are OSM Overpass rows, and those show map tagging, not whether trains run. The newest primary item, the JTA site banner dated 2026-10-30, was seen only in a search extract, and nobody checked whether it is still up. Two claims rest on unopened secondary extracts:
- The JRTC platform claim ("fenced off") comes from a Yahoo syndication.
- The claim that the JRTC has no rail service (Amtrak still at Clifford Lane) comes from an undated Action News Jax extract.
The summary also says in the present tense that NAVI vans run, but its own extracts say NAVI is to cease on January 1. That is context only.

(4) Internal consistency. I found no contradiction. Oct 30, 2026 is a Friday and Nov 2, 2026 is a Monday, which matches the quotes "pause Friday evening" and "service changes beginning Nov. 2". The Nov. 2 suspension plan also matches the Sept. 17, 2026 budget reports. The line status (suspended) and all eight station statuses (closed since 2026-10-30) are plausible but unverified, so the status I found is unknown.

Side note, also unverified: as quoted, the seven OSM nodes tagged disused still carry railway=station, so a map layer that filters on railway=station would still show them.

To verify, the session's network settings must allow www.jtafla.com (and jtafla.com), www.actionnewsjax.com, www.news4jax.com and jaxtoday.org. The web-search limit (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION) would also need raising, or the check re-run in a follow-up.
